findings.statement: The spec hard-codes ledgers without genesis, which the parallel Change #59 may make unopenable. REQ-PJ-005 fixes `typed` as four commits, with commit k at seq k and base k − 1. SCN-PJ-001 (seq 4), SCN-PJ-005 (tail 2, base 3, seq 4; tail 3) and SCN-PJ-011 (commits 1, 3, 4) depend on that numbering. REQ-PJ-005 defines `skeleton` as 'the ledger the commands write', and SCN-PJ-004 asserts that it 'holds no type record' and that every edge is at /type. Design D-1 says #59 adds a 'genesis check' to src/ledger/commit.ts, the file that holds openLedger. The archived s0-apply-checks design says #59 makes `init` write genesis (the meta-type record and the session event type, OM-L01). If that check runs at opening, neither frozen ledger opens once #59 lands. By the maintainer's decision (I-1) they are then regenerated by whichever of #59 and #60 merges its impl-PR last. Regenerating with genesis shifts the numbering of `typed`. It also gives `skeleton` type records: `core/session@1` then resolves, and step 3 runs on session events. SCN-PJ-001, SCN-PJ-004, SCN-PJ-005, SCN-PJ-011 and REQ-PJ-005 become false. Fixing them changes the `projections` spec. #60 can only do that after approval, with an I-N row and a waiver. #59 cannot do it while #60 holds AREA PJ, which lasts until #60's archive-PR merges. Design D-8 argues only that the `acts` field leaves the ledgers valid; it does not address the genesis check.
findings.recommendation: Read the spec of #59 and record the answer in design D-8. If opening will not require genesis, state in REQ-PJ-005 that both cases are kernel-0 ledgers without genesis (LG-G05) that opening accepts, and that `skeleton` is the ledger the S0 commands write before #59. If opening will require genesis, word the spec so that regenerating does not change it. `typed` becomes 'the genesis prefix that opening requires, if any, then four commits', and the scenarios count commits and seq from the first commit after that prefix. The skeleton clause of SCN-PJ-004 asserts only the records whose type does not resolve. Also have the umbrella name the Change that edits the PJ spec if a change is still needed.

findings.statement: Review 2 F-3 is closed for a repeated rev, but not for a lower rev after a higher one. REQ-PJ-001 defines `get` and `revision` by ledger order. REQ-PJ-002 removes the edges of 'the revision of the same id before it', also in ledger order. SCN-PJ-011 repeats only rev 1 after rev 1 (test/n8 and test/twice). No case writes a lower rev after a higher one. Consider an implementation that takes `get` as the highest rev, with ties going to the last record, and replaces the source with that rule. It passes every scenario. On a ledger with rev 2 and then rev 1 of one id, its `get` answers the rev-2 record and it keeps the wrong edges, against REQ-PJ-001 and REQ-PJ-002.
findings.recommendation: Add to `typed` an id written at rev 2 in commit 3 and at rev 1 in commit 4, naming different targets, for example test/n11. Have SCN-PJ-011 assert three things: `get` is the commit-4 record; `revision(id, 2)` is the commit-3 record; the referrers of the commit-3 target hold no edge from `<id>@2`.

findings.statement: Review 2 F-10 is closed for the lists but not for the edges. REQ-PJ-001 freezes the lists that `entities()` and `referrers(id)` return. It says nothing about the edge objects inside a referrers list. Suppose the view hands out its own edge objects unfrozen. A caller can then assign `edge.ref`, which changes later `referrers` answers and the `serialize` text. With copy on write (design D-3, D-4), it also changes every view that shares the edge, the views `extend` returned included. That breaks REQ-PJ-003: 'view itself stays equal to what it was'. SCN-PJ-001 checks only `entities()`.
findings.recommendation: State in REQ-PJ-001 that every edge in a list `referrers(id)` returns is frozen. Add to SCN-PJ-002 that the list `referrers("test/n2")` returns, and each edge in it, is frozen.

findings.statement: REQ-PJ-005 claims more about index.json than the file can hold. It says 'the facts SCN-PJ-001…SCN-PJ-004 and SCN-PJ-011 assert of the view hold of the parsed index.json as well'. index.json holds only `seq`, `latest` ({rev, type, hash}) and `referrers`. So most facts of SCN-PJ-001 and SCN-PJ-011 cannot hold of it: `revision(id, rev)`, frozenness, and whole records. SCN-PJ-009 checks a narrower set than REQ-PJ-005 claims. It also asserts 'the member of test/n1' for `skeleton`, which has no test/n1. And it does not say whether the negative assertions carry over to the index: 'exactly one edge from test/e1', 'no edge … from test/n5@1', 'none from test/n9@1'.
findings.recommendation: In REQ-PJ-005, replace the sentence with the content of SCN-PJ-009: `seq`, one `latest` member per entity, and the edges, positive and negative, that SCN-PJ-002…SCN-PJ-004 and SCN-PJ-011 assert of `referrers`. In SCN-PJ-009, split the facts by case. `typed` gets the test/n1 member and the named edges. `skeleton` gets one member per entity and only /type edges.

findings.statement: SCN-PJ-002 lists three edges of `referrers("test/n2")` in this sequence: from test/n1@3 at /body/pins, from test/n1@3 at /body/uses/0, from test/e1 at /body/cites. It then adds 'in the order of REQ-PJ-002'. REQ-PJ-002 orders by `from` in UTF-16 code units, and "test/e1" < "test/n1@3", so the edge from test/e1 comes first. A test that asserts the listed sequence fails on a correct implementation. SCN-PJ-009 inherits the ambiguity through 'in the same order'.
findings.recommendation: List the edges in REQ-PJ-002 order: test/e1 /body/cites; test/n1@3 /body/pins; test/n1@3 /body/uses/0. Say 'in this relative order'.

findings.statement: proposal.md (Impact) says: 'The job `test` keeps its name, so the required checks of `main` do not change.' Design D-9 and I-1 record the maintainer's decision (umbrella #44, comment 5950938286) that `projections-windows` becomes a required check of `main` after the impl-PR merges. So after the merge the required checks do change. The proposal, which is the contract, states the opposite of what the design records.
findings.recommendation: Reword the Impact line: 'the required checks of `main` do not change while the impl-PR is open; after it merges the maintainer makes `projections-windows` required (design D-9)'.

findings.statement: REQ-PJ-005 defines `skeleton` as 'the ledger the commands write' for the fixture md. By REQ-CL-003 the commands give each session event a new ULID id and an `at` from the clock. That ULID becomes every intent's `by` and appears in the `from` of the /type edges in `referrers["core/session"]`. So the case names a family of ledgers, not one set of bytes. Each run of the generator of design D-8 writes a different ledger.jsonl and index.json. On regeneration, the 'diff of index.json shown in the PR' (D-8) then changes even when no meaning has changed.
findings.recommendation: Have the generator write `skeleton` with a fixed clock and fixed ULIDs, given through the fixture ports. State it in D-8, or in REQ-PJ-005 as 'with the session ids and times of the generator', so that regenerating is reproducible and its diff shows only real changes.

findings.statement: Design D-3 justifies that `rebuild` does not check `base` with 'openLedger hands it commits whose chain it verified (LG-C04)'. Opening checks `seq` growth and the `prev` chain, not `base`. REQ-PJ-003 itself says so: 'opening a ledger does not check it (#114)'. The spec is right; only the reason given in the design is wrong.
findings.recommendation: In D-3, give the reason the spec gives: rebuild folds what opening accepts; incremental and from-scratch are equal for ledgers whose `base` follows the `seq` before it (REQ-PJ-003; #114).

proposals.change: REQ-PJ-005: after reading #59, either state that both reference ledgers are kernel-0 ledgers without genesis that opening accepts, or define `typed` as 'the genesis prefix opening requires, if any, then four commits'. In that case, phrase SCN-PJ-001, SCN-PJ-005 and SCN-PJ-011 relative to the first commit after the prefix, and limit the skeleton clause of SCN-PJ-004 to records whose type does not resolve.

Add to `typed` an id at rev 2 in commit 3 and at rev 1 in commit 4, and assert its get, revision and edges in SCN-PJ-011. In REQ-PJ-001, make the edges that referrers returns frozen, and assert it in SCN-PJ-002.

REQ-PJ-005: replace 'the facts SCN-PJ-001…SCN-PJ-004 and SCN-PJ-011 assert of the view hold of the parsed index.json' with the list SCN-PJ-009 checks. SCN-PJ-009: split its facts per case. SCN-PJ-002: list the edges of referrers("test/n2") in REQ-PJ-002 order.
Impact, CI: 'the required checks of `main` do not change while the impl-PR is open; after it merges the maintainer makes `projections-windows` required (design D-9)'.
D-8: the generator writes `skeleton` with a fixed clock and fixed ULIDs. D-8: record whether the genesis check of #59 runs at opening. D-3: correct the reason `rebuild` skips the base check.

assumptions.statement: Review 2 findings F-1, F-2, F-4, F-5, F-6, F-7, F-8 and F-11 are closed by the current text. F-9 is closed by the note in design D-8, but see F-1 here for the AREA consequence. F-3 is closed for a repeated rev and for the type cache, which now lives for one commit, but not for a lower rev after a higher one (F-2 here). F-10 is closed for lists, not for edges (F-3 here). The closures of review 1 listed in review 2 A-1 were not re-examined. Review 1 F-18 is deferred by design D-5 to the merge of the spec-PR.

The spec of s0-bootstrap (#59) is not in this worktree and was not read. F-1 infers that opening may refuse a ledger without genesis from two sources: design D-1 places a 'genesis check' in src/ledger/commit.ts (which holds openLedger), and the archived s0-apply-checks design has #59 make `init` write genesis.
Kernel and ledger behaviour was read from the main specs (kernel, ledger, cli, architecture) and from src/ledger/commit.ts, records.ts and projections/latest.ts. Nothing was executed.
